clue.text: One player's performance in colossal upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the run of letters upside down, so it reads backwards
the letters sit inside the next word of the clue, not built from meanings

parts.note: the run of letters o-l-o-s inside this word, read upward in the down entry

explanation.surface: A single musician's turn goes badly wrong in a huge flop.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading colossal backwards gives lassoloc, which holds the answer SOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo is a piece or passage performed by a single musician or player alone.

clue.text: He can ring the changes, as ten, in attack

indicators.note: one item placed inside another, so the number goes into the middle of the word for attack

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A rugby number ten in attack switches the play around to keep defenders guessing.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the number ten is the fly-half, which makes the surface sound like a match report; ringing the changes is bell-ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer whose duties traditionally include ringing the bells, and ringing the changes is a bell-ringing term.

clue.text: Official when giving a send-off for sevens player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a referee holding up a red card to send a player off
second meaning: someone playing the card game sevens, who holds cards in hand

explanation.surface: A referee dismisses a player in a rugby sevens match.
explanation.walkthrough: Sevens looks like the short form of rugby, but here it is a card game; the referee holds the red card when sending a player off.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee showing a card and a person playing a card game are both literally holding cards, giving two senses of the compound.

clue.text: Leader of Wallabies that is most off target

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the team name
id est is the Latin for 'that is', usually shortened to i.e.

explanation.surface: The Australian rugby captain is the one whose kicks stray furthest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wallabies are Australia's rugby union team. Here 'that is' is spelt out in its full Latin form rather than abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that is widest has strayed the greatest distance from the posts or goal, so it misses by most.

clue.text: Provocative statements from a nasty person, one in pack

parts.note: taken as written
git is British slang for an unpleasant person
a prop is a front-row forward in the rugby scrum, or pack

explanation.surface: Inflammatory remarks come from an unpleasant front-row forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the pack is the eight forwards; the prop is one of them. Git is a mild British insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, especially in art or literature, designed to stir up feeling and provoke action.

clue.text: Highly aggressive Kiwi activity, first of all?

definitions.text: Highly aggressive Kiwi activity, first of all?

indicators.note: the first of all the words means take the opening letter of each one

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Something fierce that New Zealanders do before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: New Zealand's All Blacks perform their war dance before a match starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is the Maori challenge dance performed by New Zealand teams, Kiwis, before kick-off, so it comes first.

clue.text: Moving back, not forward

definitions.meaning: second meaning: shy and reserved, not bold or pushy

explanation.surface: A player retreats rather than pushing ahead, as in rugby where passes must not go forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Forward reads like a direction or a rugby position, but it is the adjective meaning bold.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw, and a retiring person is diffident, the opposite of a forward, brash one.

clue.text: Like kicker that's injured in rugby match, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lame, as a hurt leg is described, kicker being a leg
second meaning: a contest of play, of which a rugby match is one instance

explanation.surface: A goal-kicker limps through the match after picking up a knock.
explanation.walkthrough: The kicker is not a player but a leg; a 'game leg' is an old-fashioned way of saying a lame one.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means lame or crippled, of a limb, and as a noun it is any match or sporting contest.

clue.text: Finished with a player on one side being dominant

parts.note: something finished is over
the article taken as written, 'with' joining it on
a wing is a rugby player who plays out on one flank

explanation.surface: A match ends with a winger dominating down one flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On one side' describes where a wing plays, confirming which player is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Overawing means intimidating others into submission, so it is close to dominating them.

clue.text: Back a time and a place for important matches

indicators.note: going back means running from the end towards the start, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Supporting a team at one time and a ground for big games.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space where contests and sporting events are staged before spectators.

clue.text: Eg captain leading little forwards in pack, say

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding, a role a captain might hold
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: The rugby captain heads up the small forwards in the scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby pack has eight forwards, so 'say' marks them as an example of a group of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: An octad is a group or set of eight, and the eight forwards of a rugby pack form one.

clue.text: With this, centre makes a short distance in final minutes

parts.words: With this, centre makes a short distance
parts.note: surface reading: a centre gains a few yards in a rugby match
setter's reading: the word centre plus four further letters can be rearranged into centimetre

explanation.surface: A rugby centre gains a few yards late in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'extra TIME': adding the letters TIME to CENTRE lets them be rearranged as CENTIMETRE, a short distance. EXTRA TIME is the added period at the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra time is the additional period played after normal time, so it supplies the last minutes of a drawn match.

clue.text: Minimal censorship? That's one way to get play restarted

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cutting of a single row of text

definitions.text: one way to get play restarted
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the rugby set piece after the ball goes into touch

explanation.surface: Only light censorship is applied before a performance resumes.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, when the ball goes off the side of the pitch, play restarts with a throw between two lines of players.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one line out is the least a censor can do, and a line-out is how rugby resumes after the ball goes into touch.

clue.text: Have score to settle between sides, so scowl

indicators.note: something set between two things has them on either side of it, enclosing it

parts.note: left, the first of the two sides
having a score to settle means owing a debt
right, the second of the two sides

explanation.surface: Someone with a grudge between rival teams glowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The two sides are left and right. Lower, rhyming with 'flower', is a variant spelling of lour.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower, also spelt lour, is to frown or look sullen, the same as to scowl.

clue.text: Work on courses about small margin of victory in rugby

parts.note: re means about or concerning

parts.words: small margin of victory in rugby
parts.note: winning by a single point is the narrowest win

explanation.surface: Practising on the training pitches about a narrow rugby win.
explanation.walkthrough: Courses are rows of bricks; repointing renews the mortar between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Repointing is renewing the mortar joints of brickwork, which is laid in horizontal rows called courses.

clue.text: Today's big event in local publication

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the day's fixture in the French capital, where the tournament was being held
second meaning: a French weekly news magazine

explanation.surface: The day's big game gets written up in the local paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared during the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France, so the day's game is a match in the French capital, which is also the name of a French news weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris Match is a well-known French weekly news magazine, a publication local to the World Cup host.

clue.text: Score on way in passionate encounter

parts.note: a try is the main score in rugby
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Scoring a try on the way during a heated match.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' puts the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic meeting between lovers, so a passionate encounter.

clue.text: Intoxicated crowd, getting over line and leading in global competition

indicators.note: a drunk stumbles about unsteadily, so these letters lurch out of order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line
a team leading is up

explanation.surface: Drunken fans pour over the touchline at the big international tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rugby World Cup is the sport's global tournament, contested by national teams from around the world.

clue.text: Thugs upset if surrounded by rugby supporters

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the short word upside down so it reads the other way

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union

indicators.note: to be surrounded is to have things on all sides, so the short word goes inside

parts.note: fans support a team
the word if, read upward

explanation.surface: Hooligans are upset if they are surrounded by rugby followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffians are violent, lawless people, the same as thugs.

clue.text: See 17
Start of rugby in old English clubs I found in study — it's compelling

indicators.note: things found in something are inside it, so the run of pieces goes within the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
OE is the abbreviation for Old English

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic paper on early rugby in old English clubs makes gripping reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The R also sits inside the old English and clubs pair, between them, before all of it goes inside CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion is the use of force or threats to make someone act, so it is what compels.

clue.text: Where you'll find beginning of game inscribed in stone

definitions.text: Where you'll find beginning of game inscribed in stone

indicators.note: lettering inscribed in something is cut into it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone

indicators.note: 'beginning of' keeps only the first letter of 'game'

parts.note: the opening letter of game

explanation.surface: The birth of the sport is commemorated on a carved stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby School has a plaque recording William Webb Ellis picking up the ball in 1823, the legendary start of the game, so the definition doubles as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The town and school of Rugby in Warwickshire are traditionally where the game of rugby football began.

clue.text: In any match he or she should play a fairly decisive role

definitions.text: In any match he or she should play a fairly decisive role

parts.words: In any match he or she should play a fairly decisive role
parts.note: surface reading: a player who is quite influential in every game
setter's reading: making decisions in a fair, impartial way, rather than being somewhat decisive

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairly' looks like 'quite', but it means 'justly': the person deciding things impartially in the match is the official in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is the official who controls a match and rules impartially on incidents.

clue.text: Leinster centre, hard worker, quick to get ready

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the middle four of these eight letters
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A Leinster centre is a hard-working player, quick to prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: Leinster is an Irish province and rugby club, and centre looks like the playing position.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant food or coffee is prepared in moments, so it is quick to make ready.

clue.text: Restrained by locks selected for team

definitions.meaning: first meaning: locked up, in jail
second meaning: picked to play, written as two words

explanation.surface: A player held by the locks in the scrum has been picked for the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks look like rugby second-row forwards, but they are the locks on a cell door.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for in prison, and someone in the side has been chosen for the team.

clue.text: Instruction to players to start fighting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a film director's call to actors to begin a take
second meaning: combat, as in soldiers seeing battle

explanation.surface: A coach orders the team to begin brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: Players are actors, not sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A director shouts the word to begin filming, and military combat is also described by it.

clue.text: Problems due to too many coaches etc dog almost half of XV

definitions.text: Problems due to too many coaches etc

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow, or tail, them
a rugby fifteen has seven backs, just under half the team

explanation.surface: A team with too many coaching staff has trouble keeping track of the backs.
explanation.walkthrough: Coaches look like trainers, but they are buses causing queues of traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailbacks are long queues of traffic, a nuisance caused by too many vehicles such as coaches on the road.

clue.text: International held in appropriate stadium

indicators.note: letters held in a phrase are contained within it, spanning the words

parts.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: An international fixture is staged at a suitable ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is an international match between national sides in rugby or cricket.

clue.text: South African starts for Boks, obviously enjoying rugby

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, one from each

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A South African supporter of the Springboks plainly loves the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boks, or Springboks, are South Africa's rugby team.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boer is a South African of Dutch descent, an Afrikaner.

clue.text: A yen that chap has to forego to become international

definitions.text: that chap has to forego to become international

parts.note: taken as written
a yen is a longing, an itch

explanation.surface: A player who wants to be capped must give up something.
explanation.walkthrough: The chap is the word CHAP: drop its H and it becomes CAP, a player capped as an international. The answer is the name of the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H, which is what must go from that word to leave a term for a capped player.

clue.text: One of two in fifteen for part of rugby match

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ...-back, either the scrum or fly position in a rugby team
second meaning: one of the two periods of forty minutes

explanation.surface: One of a pair in the team plays a part in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby fifteen has two half-backs, and a match is played in two periods.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a scrum- or fly-back player and either of the two periods into which a game is split.

clue.text: Touch, possibly? Otherwise it's five points

wordplay.note: five compass points: south, east, north, south, east

explanation.surface: Is the ball in touch, or would that be a five-point try?
explanation.walkthrough: Touch is the rugby sideline and points look like the score, but touch is one of the faculties and points are compass bearings. There are also five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch is one of the five senses, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Mature and train for Rugby, for instance? That's traditional

parts.note: mature in years means old
to school is to train or teach

explanation.surface: Grown-up training for a rugby game is the conventional approach.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby here is the English public school, founded in 1567, so it is an example of an old school too.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-school describes someone or something attached to traditional, old-fashioned ways.
